analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The changed range is head lines 808-823; it documents segmented paged KV admission behavior with no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or wire changes. The two supplied units are the base excerpt (lines 1622-1777) and the head excerpt (lines 1-415). Neither contains the changed range, so the new paragraph is visible only through the patch excerpt.

Security-relevant content in the new text: freed 64 MiB KV segments are parked per pool outside the grant, floor and ledger charge, and reinstalled for the next admission of the same size class. Parked segments are capped at min(2 GiB, slot grant/8). They are dropped on a refused admission, on a process-wide release request, and after 30 s of idleness. New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages.

Relevant threat models: T-028 (residual KV/GPU data) and TB-007 (inference engine), plus T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache). Retaining and reusing freed KV segments across requests could expose residual data to a later request if the reinstalled memory is not overwritten or zeroed before reads. The documentation only describes this; it is not code evidence of a vulnerability. Paged attention normally writes before reading. Retained memory sits outside the ledger, so it could weaken the memory-budget accounting that T-029 and DoS considerations rely on. The cap and the release triggers bound this.

No finding is raised because only docs changed. The implementing code (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, PagedKVGroup.swift, KVPoolReclaimer) was not supplied. A reviewer of the code change should check: (1) that reused parked segments cannot leak one request's or tenant's KV into another, and that stale data is never read; (2) that the off-ledger 2 GiB parked memory cannot cause an OOM or over-commit; (3) that cross-scope isolation is unaffected. The env switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP are new documented knobs. The threat model should note them if the code lands.
